title: Separate public API inputs from raw native binding inputs
applies_when: A Python/Rust or other cross-language regression proposes direct scalar inputs to a public wrapper that converts an object before calling the native binding, such as LanceDB read_consistency_interval timedelta to seconds.
lesson: Trace the wrapper conversion before choosing the reproduction. In LanceDB, public connection APIs accept timedelta and call total_seconds(); passing a float there fails in Python before the Rust Duration conversion and cannot reproduce its panic. A negative timedelta reaches that conversion through supported public sync/async and namespace paths. Test NaN, infinity and overflow separately at the raw PyO3 binding, and label that scope explicitly. Exercise the actual namespace client, not an arbitrary stand-in. Use identical committed regressions with separately rebuilt native baselines/candidates, fresh imports and valid None/zero/positive controls. An invalid proposed test need not invalidate the underlying bug: refine the input and test the real boundary.
avoid_when: Do not claim that every raw-binding input is reachable from the public API. Other wrappers, versions and serializers may admit different inputs; inspect them independently. Source-tree test metadata does not qualify wheel/editable packaging, and focused native passes do not establish full CI, live cloud or performance. A published PR is not maintainer acceptance. This advice is a scoped reuse of the broader consumer-contract lesson, not a rule to reject all low-level validation defects.

evidence.note: Public connect_async declares Optional[timedelta] and invokes total_seconds before lancedb_connect. This is the input-conversion contract, not a runtime result.

Submitted native validation fix with public negative timedelta and raw-binding non-finite/overflow tests: unchanged native baseline 22 failed/4 passed, rebuilt candidate 26 passed plus two existing regressions. Source-tree test version metadata was supplied explicitly; full packaging/cloud CI and performance were not tested.
